metadata.title: The drop that wasn’t.
metadata.description: Paid conversion appears to have fallen overnight. Separate a behavior change from a reporting error, then publish a verified explanation.
metadata.briefing: Welcome to Daylight Studio, a fictional commerce team. Daily paid conversion appears to fall from 60% to 40%. The store uses America/Los_Angeles. Maya can discuss source ingestion and Leo knows the business-date requirement. Inspect timestamped sources and transformations, repair the materialized report and publish a verified simulated stakeholder update. The dataset is frozen: logical ticks never create payments. A winter boundary fixture tests the transformation but never contributes to incident totals. Cap: 20 simulated minutes. Score: diagnosis 20, outcome 40, verification 20, structured communication 10, judgment 10.
objectives: Use the named store time zone
Correct both affected daily report rows
Preserve 90 orders and $9,000 across affected dates
Publish a current correct verified report

teammates.name: Maya
teammates.persona: Be concise, grounded, and explicit about missing evidence. Never execute actions.
teammates.welcome: The ingestion run completed. Let’s inspect the source timestamps before blaming customer behavior.
teammates.fallback: I can confirm ingestion status, but we need to open the sources to discuss the actual records.

teammates.name: Leo
teammates.persona: Be concise, grounded, and explicit about missing evidence. Never execute actions.
teammates.welcome: The business expects store-local reporting dates. Let’s inspect how each dataset is grouped.
teammates.fallback: The business-date requirement is store local. Open the transforms before we infer their implementation.

artifacts.title: Session and payment sources
artifacts.body:
HISTORICAL INCIDENT EVIDENCE · frozen affected dates
Store zone: America/Los_Angeles. Every order is $100. Ingestion completed with no missing or duplicate payment IDs.
paid_at_utc,orders,revenue
2025-07-15T17:00:00Z,40,$4000
2025-07-16T02:00:00Z,20,$2000
2025-07-16T17:00:00Z,30,$3000
Local-date sessions: July 15 = 100; July 16 = 50.
Baseline July 14 conversion = 60% is context only and excluded from affected-date totals. Affected-date totals: 90 paid orders, $9000.

artifacts.title: Business-date transformations
artifacts.body:
HISTORICAL INCIDENT EVIDENCE · t=0
Sessions → America/Los_Angeles business date → group by date.
Payments → extract UTC calendar date → group by date.
Join both aggregates on date.
Current materialized report: July 15 = 40/100, 40%, $4000; July 16 = 50/50, 100%, $5000.
Changing a transformation does not rebuild the materialized table. A rebuild records the source and transformation fingerprints. A fixed UTC-7 offset matches summer only; the named zone follows seasonal transitions.

artifacts.title: Summer and winter boundary tests
artifacts.body:
ISOLATED TEST-FIXTURE OUTPUT SPECIFICATION
Summer: July 16, 2025 02:00Z → July 15 in America/Los_Angeles (UTC-7).
Winter: January 16, 2025 07:30Z → January 15 in America/Los_Angeles (UTC-8).
The winter example is a separate fixture, never an incident payment.
Verify both boundary dates and both materialized daily rows. Expected report: July 15 = 60/100, 60%, $6000; July 16 = 30/50, 60%, $3000. Totals remain 90 orders / $9000. Passing aggregate totals alone cannot establish correct daily attribution.

facts.text: Stakeholders expect store-local business dates in America/Los_Angeles.
Sources contain 40 payments at July 15 17:00Z, 20 at July 16 02:00Z, and 30 at July 16 17:00Z, with no duplicates or missing records.
Sessions group by store-local date; payments currently extract UTC date. Configuration changes require a materialized rebuild.
Summer and winter boundaries use different offsets. The named zone maps both fixtures to the previous local date; the winter fixture is excluded from incident revenue.

action_catalog.description: Repeat the successful ingestion process without changing grouping or source data.

action_catalog.label: Verify affected-date totals
action_catalog.description: Check report freshness, 90 unique orders, and $9,000 across affected dates.

action_catalog.label: Test summer and winter boundaries
action_catalog.description: Check isolated seasonal boundary fixtures and both current daily rows.

action_catalog.label: Publish stakeholder report
action_catalog.description: Store an immutable simulated report snapshot. Incorrect or unverified publications are recorded.

diagnosis_choices.label: Payment ingestion dropped a group of orders
The joined datasets use inconsistent time-zone date buckets
Customer conversion truly declined on July 15

rubric.explanation: Sessions use store-local business dates while payments used UTC dates. Twenty late-local-evening July 15 payments landed in July 16 UTC. Normalize payment timestamps to America/Los_Angeles before extracting the date, rebuild the report, and verify both totals and summer/winter boundaries before publication. A fixed UTC-7 offset fits July but fails winter; total revenue alone cannot prove attribution.

hints.text: Compare the source timestamp groups with the report’s two daily rows.
Compare how each transform extracts a date, then check whether one fixed offset works for both boundary fixtures.
